findings.detail: ROOT CAUSE PROVEN this tick, three-step reproduction. (1) task_list_held(kind='session-presence') returned count:0 thirty seconds after cowork-tick-preflight.sh Step 2 had supposedly registered presence with ttl_seconds:1800. (2) The tool is not at fault: a manual task_claim of session-presence:7be6b4cd-... returned claimed:true (a FRESH claim, so no row existed) and the very next task_list_held returned it, count:1. (3) The script's shape is the fault: cowork-tick-preflight.sh:214-216 builds payload as a jq OBJECT -- payload:{agent_id:'cowork-dispatcher', host:$host}. Reproduced the rejection directly: task_claim with an object payload returns MCP -32602 Zod invalid_type, 'Expected string, received object', path ['payload']. The script's own comment at line 228 then swallows it -- 'Transport error on the claim itself falls through here too - presence never gates.' So the claim has been failing on EVERY tick and the never-gate fallback hides it completely. Consequences: (a) Phase A.5 presence roster is permanently empty and advisory-useless; (b) SERIOUS -- .claude/skills/cron-cowork-team/SKILL.md Step 1b.1 uses session-presence as its PRIMARY staleness oracle, and 'no presence row' is its DEAD branch, which then calls task_force_release_orphan on a peer's cron-registration:cowork-team marker and re-registers. An always-empty roster classifies every LIVE peer as dead, so any re-arm can steal a live peer's registration and double-arm the dispatcher. This is the mechanism behind the previously-recorded 'empty roster / false-dead' incidents; the fix is one character class -- stringify the payload (payload MUST be a JSON string, same constraint already documented for every other task_claim call site). Zone scripts/ -> developer. Audit sibling call sites in scripts/agents-flow/ for the same object-payload shape.

Consequence of the 09:30Z hold, now measured. cowork-tick-preflight.sh:360-365 computes the SILENT gate as slots_empty && one_shots_empty && signal_count==0, where signal_count counts NEW rows addressed to the SSOT cowork recipient set. The 7 undeliverable to=po rows I held at NEW therefore force verdict=WORK on every subsequent tick: 09:30Z and 09:45Z both came back WORK with slots:[] and one_shots:[], driven by new_signals:7 alone. Two full dispatch bodies run for zero dispatchable work, and this repeats every 15 minutes indefinitely. This reframes the underlying defect: the drain's mark-NEW->READ is not merely lossy bookkeeping, it is LOAD-BEARING for the SILENT gate, and there is no third state for 'undeliverable but still visible'. So the two available behaviours are (a) mark READ -> row cold-evicts unseen at 24h, PO never selects it, SILENT gate works; (b) hold NEW -> row stays visible but PO still has no cowork slot to be routed to, and the dispatcher can never go silent. Neither delivers. A real fix needs either a po delivery path or a distinct terminal status. Rows unchanged this tick: same 8 NEW (7 to=po, 1 to=ops out of scope), 85 already in READ addressed to po.

Recording a decision reversed mid-tick. Given two escalation-worthy findings and CLAUDE.md's 'never ask user - spawn po for decisions', I ran the mandatory PRE-CLAIM sequence (Phase A orphan-signal probe: 0 locks, clean; Phase A.5 roster: empty, per the defect above; Phase B: intent:po:cowork-signalqueue-po-jam-and-preflight-presence-claim-break-20260824 claimed true) and then did NOT spawn, releasing the intent lock cleanly (released:1). Reason: work-tick.md Step 0a's own branch for po-addressed rows is 'route to matching agent slot at Step 5 OR log for PO', and there is no po cowork slot, so the authorised branch is log. This tick matched ZERO slots, so no Step 5 fan-out spawn is authorised either. Escalation therefore goes out as this telemetry envelope (to: po) rather than a dispatch. Noting it because a PRE-CLAIM sequence that ends in no spawn otherwise looks like an aborted or collided dispatch in the lock history.
